method: Started from 2,594 priced Kalshi legs in the next 36 hours. Kept legs priced 30–85¢ with edge of about −2.5 or better and no flags, one per game, and checked them against today's 140 newly collected expert picks and Polymarket top-trader positions. A leg stayed only if at least two of top-trader money, a published pick or model, and concrete matchup/injury reasoning agreed, with nothing disagreeing. Dropped for conflicts: Kings +6.5 (top traders $15.6k on Sacramento, but TheLines and BettingPros have Suns −6.5); Texans −13.5 (top traders on Houston, but SI, Covers and The Sports Geek take the Colts +9.5 to +12.5); Cavaliers −4.5 (Dimers and top traders on Cleveland, Covers has Memphis ML); Wizards +6.5 (Dimers and Covers on Washington, but top traders back Toronto's moneyline); Hawks/Thunder Under (Predictem Under, top traders on the Over); Celtics/Nuggets (Lineups has Boston, Covers Denver); Hawks +4.5 (Bang The Book has OKC); Pacers +6.5 (Covers has Houston ML); UMass −2.5 (three outlets, but the small top-trader money is on Akron); Houston/Florida, UConn/Arizona and both MLS wild-card games (experts split). Thursday games (TNF aside) had almost no published previews yet, so all seven legs are Wednesday night; the ladder is shorter than usual rather than padded with unsupported legs.
honest: Every leg costs slightly more than its fair price (edge about −1 to −2.5¢ each), so expected return is slightly negative, and it gets worse with each leg you add.

ladder.label: Buffalo Bulls −2.5
ladder.why: Buffalo has won five straight and covered all six MAC games (7-3 overall). Central Michigan runs 41 times a game but passes for only about 127 yards, and its run defense ranks 136th in success rate against Buffalo's 1,110-yard back Messiah Burch. Three outlets have Buffalo, and top-trader money is all on this side.

ladder.label: New Orleans Pelicans +7.5
ladder.why: Dimers' model makes the Pelicans a 54% cover at +7 and projects Pistons 117–110, and Covers likes New Orleans outright with Herb Jones on Cade Cunningham and Zion inside. Top traders hold about $5.7k on the Pelicans at this line against $0.8k on Detroit.

ladder.label: New Jersey Devils
ladder.why: New Jersey is 9-2-0 at home with strong 5-on-5 shot and expected-goal shares, while Montreal is dealing with injuries and scored once in each of its last two games. Three outlets pick the Devils, and the small top-trader money is on New Jersey.

ladder.label: Colorado Avalanche
ladder.why: Utah has lost six straight with an .891 5-on-5 save percentage and a 69% penalty kill, while Colorado's goalie Blackwood is +4.2 goals saved above expected over his last eight. Five outlets take Colorado even without MacKinnon and Makar, which is why it's a near coin-flip price. No top-trader money either way.

ladder.label: Under 236.5
ladder.why: Dimers' model has the Under 237.5 in Bulls–Nets, and top traders hold about $1.3k on the Under at the next line up (238.5) against $61 on the Over. No top-trader money at this exact line.

ladder.label: Boston Bruins +1.5
ladder.why: Boston has won six straight meetings and scores 3.55 goals a game while allowing 2.60, against Detroit's 2.62 scored. Two outlets pick the Bruins to win outright; this leg only needs them not to lose by two or more. No top-trader money either way.

ladder.label: Kansas Jayhawks
ladder.why: Dimers' model projects Kansas 80–70 and FanDuel Research cites Kansas' rebounding and interior edge. Both lay 8.5–9.5 points, so this leg only needs the straight-up win. No top-trader money either way.
